answer: Graded identity decay curve.** Each identity's messaging weight decays over time unless refreshed by a small fee; the delta between refresh cost and earned value must stay positive for honest agents. A juniper-tier identity (new, low history) pays a higher refresh rate than established ones, so mass-registering identities incurs compounding costs before any pulse of activity yields returns. Attacker cost scales superlinearly with identity count: N identities cost roughly N^1.5 in refresh fees, making large sybil farms economically unviable without a hard gate.
